why: In kdoc mode a wrapped line (text containing ♢/%W that exceeds the column limit) would be continued at indentLevel+2 instead of indentLevel; only file-comment wrapping is tested, not kdoc wrapping.
A long kdoc with a ♢ wrap point would lose the ' * ' prefix on its continuation line; no test wraps kdoc text (only a // file comment).
lastDotIndex==0 would only add "" to memberImportNames, and it is only checked against ClassName.canonicalName, which is never empty, so nothing observable changes.

A line that starts with ♢ at indentLevel 0 and outside kdoc (e.g. the expression body of a top-level fun 'return 1 +\n♢2') leaves segments ["", "2"], so the mutant skips the ensureTrailingNewline newline; this is contrived but reachable.
A digit or other non-start identifier character after position 0 (e.g. newName("foo1")) would get an underscore inserted ('foo_1'); NameAllocatorTest only has a leading digit.
No production caller passes a 5th argument (they are all 2- or 4-arg with non-null receivers), but a direct test like 'e'.isOneOf('a','b','c','d','e') on this internal helper would expose it.
No production caller passes a 6th argument, but a direct test of the internal helper with a match in t6 would return false under the mutant.
If the '"' branch is skipped, '"' falls through to else -> c.toString(), which returns the same "\"" string.

After the escape chain, any string containing an illegal character ('.', ';', etc. are none of them JavaIdentifierPart) is backtick-wrapped, so failIfEscapeInvalid can never throw and forcing validation changes nothing.
failIfEscapeInvalid is a no-op after escapeIfNotJavaIdentifier has wrapped every string that contains an illegal character, so inverting the validate flag is unobservable.
Removing failIfEscapeInvalid is unobservable: its require is always satisfied because an escaped string counts as alreadyEscaped and an unescaped one has no illegal characters.
An all-underscore string cannot start with a backtick and so can never be alreadyEscaped, so !alreadyEscaped() is always true here.
On the JVM every isJavaIdentifierStart char is also isJavaIdentifierPart, so including the first char in the any{} check cannot change the result.
CodeBlock.replaceAll uses String.replace with a literal (not a regex), and '[⇥|⇤]' can never appear inside a format part (⇥/⇤ are always split into their own parts), so the map is a no-op.
Applying replaceAll("[⇥|⇤]", "") to non-inline members is a no-op because that literal string never occurs in any format part.
Skipping the replaceAll for inline annotations is unobservable because literal replacement of '[⇥|⇤]' never matches any format part.

Any length-1 last part such as "
" would be treated as a placeholder, e.g. kdoc CodeBlock.of("%L
", "text") through ensureEndsWithNewLine would give 'text

' instead of 'text
'.
isPlaceholder is only called on the last part of a trim()'d block, and trim() strips trailing single-char placeholders, so the first disjunct is always false.
Format parts that start with ⇥⇤«» are always exactly length 1 (the parser splits them out), and the trimmed last part is never empty in practice, so the check stays false.
No format part longer than 1 char can start with a single-char placeholder, and after trim() a length-1 placeholder cannot be last, so the result is unchanged except on an unreachable empty part.
Any length-1 non-placeholder last part (e.g. "\n" in kdoc "%L\n" with a String arg) would be treated as a placeholder and the String arg trimmed instead, which duplicates the trailing newline.
Format parts that start with '%' are always exactly 2 chars (literal parts never begin with '%'), so dropping length == 2 does not change the result.
lastDotIndex==0 would only add "" to memberImportNames, which is compared to ClassName canonical names that are never empty, so nothing observable changes.
A class with two type aliases, or a property followed by a type alias, would lose the blank line between members; the only addTypeAlias test has a single alias as the first member.

A body like 'return «1»' followed by a stray » (e.g. addStatement("return «1»") plus a second statement) makes the original report an unmatched close and return null, while the mutant's count goes negative and it emits an expression body.
For '«a»»' after a return prefix, the original sees the second » at count 0 and returns true, but the mutant's count only grows, so it wrongly allows an expression body.
A KTypeParameter with a real upper bound (e.g. T : Number) would get an extra Any? in its public bounds list, which changes equality and output; this KType path has no tests.
An unbounded KTypeParameter would end up with empty bounds instead of [Any?], which is visible via TypeVariableName.bounds and equality.
parentSubcommandsVarName is only read in the !isTopLevel branch, so what it holds for top-level commands is never used.
A subcommand whose help contains an apostrophe would produce an unescaped ' inside -d '...' in the fish script; the tests' subcommands have no help.
A subcommand with non-blank help would lose its -d description; no fish test gives a subcommand help text.
A command with no options that have dash-prefixed names (e.g. helpOptionNames empty and only arguments, or only '/x'-style options) would still print a '## Options for' header.
An option whose names all lack a '-' prefix (e.g. option("/x") or "+x", which clikt allows) would emit a bare 'complete -c c' line instead of being skipped.
A single-dash long option name like '-foo' would be emitted with '-s' instead of '-o'; tests only use '-h' and '--' names.
An argument declared with help text would lose its -d description in the fish script; the test arguments have no help.

paramName is a public mutable String? on UsageError, so NoSuchOption("--x").apply { paramName = null }.formatMessage(...) returns a message in the original but throws NPE under the mutant; the framework itself never sets null.

With a help formatter that styles option names (MordantHelpFormatter with ANSI, or a custom styleOptionName), the 'Did you mean' possibilities would come out unstyled; tests only use the plain formatter.
If an option is mistyped at the parent with a close match there (possibilities non-empty) and a subcommand also has that exact option, the mutant gives the subcommand hint instead of 'Did you mean'.
An unknown option matched by no subcommand, where some subcommand has any option (e.g. --help), would get a bogus 'hint: sub has an option' message instead of plain 'no such option'.

The custom or default help text of SuspendingCompletionCommand would disappear from the parent's --help listing and from the completion scripts; the test only checks that the output contains the shell name and 'foo'.
Running SuspendingCompletionCommand as a root command (no parent context) would throw an NPE instead of printing its own completion script.
ChainedCompletionCommand's help text would vanish from the parent help listing and the completion script descriptions, and no test checks that help.
Running ChainedCompletionCommand as a standalone root command would throw an NPE instead of generating completion for itself.
